wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Goa
wars.outcome: Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510, the Bijapuris countered, and it was recaptured on 25 November 1510; Portuguese until 1961.
wars.note: S7 adds the aid of the Hindu privateer Timoja.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Malacca
wars.outcome: Albuquerque had captured Malacca by July 1511; the Dutch took it in 1641.
wars.note: The page gives no campaign detail.

wars.name: Dutch–Portuguese War

zones.text: Dutch Brazil: Olinda and Recife from 1630 to 1654
the Portuguese Gold Coast, Dutch in 1637 and 1642
Ceylon: Batticaloa 1639, Galle 1640, Colombo 1656, the last Portuguese out in 1658

wars.outcome: The Portuguese expelled the Dutch from Recife in 1654 and retook Luanda on 15 August (1648); the Dutch kept Elmina (1637), the Gold Coast (1642), Malacca (1641), Ceylon (1658) and the Malabar coast (1663). By the Treaty of The Hague of 6 August 1661 the Dutch ceded Brazil and Portugal ceded Ceylon and the Maluku Islands and paid eight million guilders.
wars.note: The first decades (Amboina 1605, Hormuz 1622, Salvador 1624-1625, Pernambuco 1630, Elmina 1637) fell in the Iberian Union, when Cliopatria draws the Portuguese lands in its Spanish Empire row; the ledger of this dossier starts the losses in 1641. The page lists Ceylon both as taken by 1658 and as ceded in 1661. S9 dates the Dutch at Luanda 1640-1648, S6 1641-1648.

wars.name: Portuguese Restoration War
wars.outcome: João IV was acclaimed on 1 December 1640; "Spain recognized Portugal's sovereignty and made peace on 13 February 1668"; Ceuta stayed Spanish (S11) and was formally ceded in exchange (S1).
wars.note: No overseas border moved in this war; the home front is the Kingdom of Portugal's (eu-12). The page does not name the Treaty of Lisbon.

wars.name: Battle of Mbwila
wars.outcome: "Portugal defeated the Kongo Kingdom in the Battle of Mbwila on 29 October, 1665."
wars.note: No border change is on the page; Cliopatria's Kongo row (af-06) ends in 1669.

wars.name: Guaraní War

zones.text: the seven Jesuit mission towns east of the Uruguay River

wars.outcome: Spanish and Portuguese forces crushed the Guaraní at Caiboaté on 10 February 1756 and occupied the missions; the Treaty of Madrid was annulled in 1761 and Spain regained them.
wars.note: The page says the Portuguese held the missions until 1759 and also that Spain and Portugal annulled the treaty at El Pardo in 1761.

wars.name: Fantastic War (Spain and Portugal, 1762–1763)

zones.text: Colonia del Sacramento, captured by Spain

wars.outcome: Spain captured Colonia del Sacramento and "the treaty later required Spain to return it".
wars.note: The page gives neither the day of the capture nor the name of the treaty.

wars.name: Anglo-Portuguese capture of French Guiana
wars.outcome: "In 1809, an Anglo-Portuguese naval squadron took French Guiana" and gave it to the Portuguese in Brazil; a Portuguese presence "remained until 1817".
wars.note: No month or campaign is on the page; the Cliopatria shape includes French Guiana 1809-1814 and drops it in 1815.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Banda Oriental

zones.text: the Banda Oriental, later the province of Cisplatina

wars.outcome: The Portuguese invaded in August 1816, occupied Montevideo on 20 January 1817, won at Tacuarembó after a three-year struggle and annexed the province as Cisplatina in 1821 (assembly of 18 July 1821).
wars.note: The infobox says annexed 1817, the body 1821. Uruguay became independent from Brazil after the Cisplatine War (preliminary peace of 27 August 1828), outside this dossier.

certainty.note: Forts, factories, claims and the Brazilian interior drawn as uti possidetis are approximate throughout. The Río de la Plata frontier is sharp after the Treaty of Madrid line (1750, annulled 1761), the First Treaty of San Ildefonso (1 October 1777) and the Treaty of El Pardo (11 March 1778) with their Boundary Commission; Goa, Daman and Diu are small sharp enclaves.

Angola and Mozambique are drawn within treaty frontiers (1885-1886 agreements, Anglo-Portuguese Treaty 1891, award of 1905), but effective occupation came only between 1895 and the early 20th century (S8, S9), so the interior is a claim.

notes:
ONE STATE, TWO CLIOPATRIA ROWS. Cliopatria's "Portuguese Empire" (1502-1823, 48 shapes: Brazil, Africa and the Atlantic) and "Portuguese Colonies" (1564-1910, 32 shapes: Goa, Macau, Timor, Ceylon until 1658) share Wikidata Q200464 and the Wikipedia article "Portuguese Empire", and both are members of the umbrella (Portuguese Empire). They are the Atlantic and the Asian halves of one state, so this is one dossier under the earlier slug with both Names in cliopatria_names and all 80 shapes reviewed. The group sa-06 owns the slug portuguese-colonies: it should not write a second dossier (or should make it a pointer), and the colour agent should give portuguese-colonies the colour of portuguese-empire. The other components of the umbrella, Portuguese Africa (1507-1581, af groups) and Portuguese Ceylon (1507-1686, sa-06), are also parts of this state in Cliopatria's own model; they are not mine to edit.

LIFE SPAN. The infobox says "c. 1415 to 1999" (S1). The dossier starts in 1415 at Ceuta (as the Tang example starts in 618 where Cliopatria starts in 623) with new keyframes for 1415-1501, and ends in 1910, where Cliopatria's Colonies row ends and its Portuguese Republic row (1911-1925, eu-20; then Estado Novo 1926-2024, eu-21) takes over the same overseas territories. The empire did not end in 1910: the dissolve event is a regime change, so the colour agent may prefer to treat the Republic and Estado Novo as continuations (rule 2). Neither of the two rows draws Angola or Mozambique in 1824-1910 (the Colonies row has Asia only, the empire row ends in 1823); four new keyframes (1824, 1885, 1891, 1895) restore them from S1, S8 and S9.

OVERLAPS TO RESOLVE IN THE COMPILE STEP. (1) Cliopatria's Kingdom of Portugal shapes already hold Ceuta (1415 shape), Madeira and the Azores (1450 shape) and, in 1502, also Cape Verde, Tangier, Safi, São Tomé and Fernando Po, which its Portuguese Empire 1502 shape holds too; the pre-1502 events and keyframes here repeat Ceuta, Madeira and the Azores because S1 dates them (1415, 1419, 1427) and they are the empire's birth. eu-12's kingdom-of-portugal dossier should decide which row draws them; the Portuguese Empire is the lighter green of the same family. (2) During the Iberian Union Cliopatria draws the Portuguese overseas lands (Brazil, Angola, Mozambique, Goa, Ceylon, Timor, Malacca) inside its Spanish Empire row from 1582 to 1639 and Madeira and the Azores inside the Iberian Union row; the empire has no shape of its own in those years except the 3-cell Northern Province patch, a stray 1619-1621 shape that is not Portuguese, and Portuguese Ceylon. The ledger records a loss to spanish-empire in 1581 and a gain in 1640 (a personal union with Portuguese autonomy, S11): spanish-empire (am-06-b/c) needs the matching events or a personal-union tint. Losses of the union years (Amboina 1605, Hormuz 1622, Salvador 1624-1625, Pernambuco 1630, Elmina 1637) are therefore not in this ledger, only in the Dutch-Portuguese War entry.
